editorial:
Imagine waking up in a hospital with no clue who you are, only to find out you are the most hated man in the country. That is exactly what happens to Keisuke Kuroda, the Prime Minister of Japan, after someone literally throws a rock at his head. You get to follow him as he tries to navigate his high-pressure job without knowing a single thing about his own past or his politics. The vibe is a great mix of awkward comedy and heartfelt drama, as you watch a man basically get a second chance to be a decent person while his three stressed-out secretaries try to keep the secret from the public.

What really makes this work is the acting and the funny tension of the secret. The pacing is smooth, though some of the political talk can feel a bit slow. You will love seeing him make decisions based on kindness instead of cold politics. If you want the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those crisp visuals, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a perfect pick if you enjoy stories about people rediscovering themselves in weird situations.
endingExplained: In the end, Kuroda decides to stay the Prime Minister even after his memory returns. He realizes that the man he was before the accident was cold and uncaring. Instead of going back to his old ways, he chooses to keep the kindness and honesty he discovered while he had amnesia. He uses his power to actually help people, proving that he has truly changed for the better. He ends up being a leader people can actually trust.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves fish-out-of-water stories and light political comedies.
